Gate(docs): PRINCIPLES + ARCHITECTURE consistent after edit

description:
Add a new principle to docs/PRINCIPLES.md — 'Everyone uses the front door' — stating that the `lernie` CLI is the sole control plane: when one procedure invokes another, the invocation is a CLI call (exec'd subprocess), never an in-process sidechannel. Subagent dispatch is `exec(lernie dispatch ...)`. The harness is its own first-class consumer of the same CLI surface external callers use.

Also add a short section to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md under the dispatch/invocation material making the mechanical claim explicit and forbidding in-process sidechannels between procedures.

Three named motivations:
1. Integration testability — every inter-procedure edge is observable as a CLI call.
2. Embeddability — lernie can be a component in other tools rather than a monolith.
3. Clean architectural paths — operational atomicity, no back-channel inter-procedure communication.

Terms: 'procedure' is already defined (ARCH §404 passage near workflow bindings). 'Control plane' used as borrowed term-of-art, not coined. Reject 'first tier interface' phrasing; drop 'front door' as load-bearing term (use it only as the principle's tagline).
title: Codify 'Everyone uses the front door' principle
